learning_outcomes.text: The fundamental equations of flow motion can be derived in differential form.
Analytically can solve simple flow problems.
Can derive boundary layer equations and apply them to some problems.
Can analyze flow and forces acting on the immersed bodies.

syllabus_topics: DIFFERENTIAL ANALYSIS OF FLUID MOTION: Derivation of continuity equation. Stream function for two-dimensional incompressible flows.
DIFFERENTIAL ANALYSIS OF FLUID MOTION: Motion of fluid elements (kinematics), derivation of momentum equation.
DIFFERENTIAL ANALYSIS OF FLUID MOTION: Motion of fluid elements (kinematics), derivation of momentum equation.
INCOMPRESSIBLE INVISCID FLOW: Irrotational flow. Bernoulli equation for irrotational flow. Velocity potential and stream function.
INCOMPRESSIBLE INVISCID FLOW: Elementary plane flows. Superposition of plane flows.
DIMENSIONAL ANALYSIS AND SIMILITUDE: Introduction. Buckingham Pi theorem. Determination of Pi groups.
DIMENSIONAL ANALYSIS AND SIMILITUDE: Dimensionless groups of significance in fluid mechanics. Flow similarity and model studies.
DIMENSIONAL ANALYSIS AND SIMILITUDE: Dimensionless groups of significance in fluid mechanics. Flow similarity and model studies. EXPERIMENT I
BOUNDARY LAYER: The boundary layer concept, boundary layer thicknesses.
BOUNDARY LAYER: Laminar flat-plate boundary layer: Exact solution. Momentum integral equations.
FLOW ABOUT IMMERSED BODIES: Drag and lift on surfaces parallel and normal to flow. EXPERIMENT II
FLOW ABOUT IMMERSED BODIES: Flow over cylinder and sphere: Drag and lift forces. Flow over different geometrical shapes.
COMPRESSIBLE FLOW: Introduction. Analysis of steady one-dimensional compressible flow. Fanno line and Rayleigh line.
COMPRESSIBLE FLOW: Introduction. Analysis of steady one-dimensional compressible flow. Fanno line and Rayleigh line.
bibliography: Mechanics of Fluids, M. C. Potter and D. C. Wiggert, Prentice Hall.
